headline: The front-end shock has left the bond market: this is now a dollar squeeze, and Brazil and bitcoin are where it is breaking.
summary: Yesterday the story was the 2-year's 17bp shock. Today the shock has travelled. The rates composite is still the ugliest single number at -40, but the dollar composite at -44 has taken over as the transmission mechanism, and it is doing damage outside the US. DXY is 103.25 at the 100th percentile of its year, EURUSD 1.1055 at the 0th, USDCHF at the 100th. The fracture point is Brazil: USDBRL +1.5% today to 5.6656, +12.7% in a month at a 3.62 z-score with acceleration z=2.81 — the most extreme reading anywhere on the board, and it is still speeding up. EWZ is -25.9% on the month (z=-3.37), Bovespa -17.2%, Argentina -18.1% and pinned at the 0th percentile. This is not generic EM: USDMXN was -0.1% today, Mexico's IPC sits at the 98th percentile +7.2% on the month, and INDA is +9.1% with the Sensex at z=2.89. The dollar is picking off the weak balance sheets one at a time.

The second thing that changed overnight: bitcoin lost 70,000. BTC 69,152, -3.1% on the day and -15.2% on the month; ETH broke 2,000 to 1,955 (-19.1%); SOL -22.6%; IBIT -4.5%; MSTR -24.8% on the month; COIN -28.1% and at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range. That is the same real-yield problem — DFII10 at 2.78, up 12bp and sitting 24.2% above its 200-day — hitting everything whose valuation is a discount rate. Note the divergence inside the hard-asset trade: gold actually stabilised today, +0.2% to 3,893.8, but the equity proxies did not get the memo on the prior tape — GDX -4.0%, GDXJ -4.7%, NEM -4.9%. Miners are now cheaper relative to a metal that has stopped falling, which is the first crack of light in that complex rather than a fresh capitulation signal.

Beneath the index, the rotation that absorbed the AI unwind is genuinely tired. RSP/SPY printed z=3.10 and then gave back 0.5%; IWM/SPY -1.3%; Russell 2000 -1.7%; JETS -3.8%, XRT -1.8%, ITB -1.8% — the exact one-month winners (+8.4%, +7.5%, +10.8%) taking the hit. What is still working is defensive and boring: SPLV z=1.92 turning up, XLP z=2.04, XLV +10.7% on the month with relative strength +13.8%, LLY +22.4%, MCD z=3.04 with acceleration z=3.01, HD z=2.51, LMT z=2.49, UPS z=2.09. High beta versus low vol is -15.5% on the month at z=-2.43 and still accelerating lower. Meanwhile VIX itself fell 1.6% to 18.40 and is -28.2% on the week, but VIX3M rose 4.3% and the VIX/VIX3M ratio is 0.9322 and turning up at z=1.05 — hedging demand is moving out the curve, not disappearing.

Keep two offsetting facts in view. The economy is fine: claims 200k, continuing claims 1.697m at the 1st percentile, unemployment 4.1% and falling, JOLTS 7,523 (+4.6%), industrial production +0.63 and capacity utilisation at the 100th percentile — growth pulse +2. Index credit is also fine: HY OAS -4bp to 3.30, IG -1bp to 0.90, BBB -1bp, HYG/IEF +0.3%, BKLN at the 97.5th percentile. But the tail keeps paying: CCC spreads +19bp to 13.30, +77bp on the month and +445bp year-to-date at the 95th percentile, against an IG index that tightened. And the cyclical commodity complex disagrees with the payroll data — copper -6.7% on the month and rolling over, COPX -15.9%, FCX -16.3%, XME -8.2%, REMX -11.4%, DBC z=-1.75. Funding cost, not demand, is the binding constraint; that is why the right expressions today are dispersion and the dollar, not index direction.

good.text: The labour and activity data remain unambiguously solid: initial claims 200k, continuing claims 1.697m at the 1st percentile of the year, unemployment 4.1% and falling, JOLTS 7,523 (+4.6%), industrial production +0.63 and capacity utilisation at the 100th percentile. This is not a growth scare.

Index-level credit refuses to crack: HY OAS -4bp to 3.30, IG -1bp to 0.90, BBB -1bp to 1.12, HYG/IEF +0.3% and turning up, BKLN at the 97.5th percentile. The investment-grade bid is intact even as the equity tape chops.

Europe and India keep compounding through the dollar move: DAX 26,732 at the 99th percentile and +5.7% on the month, CAC +6.1% (z=1.29), Sensex +12.1% at z=2.89 with acceleration 2.59, INDA +9.1% with relative strength +12.1%, Mexico's IPC at the 98th percentile.

The week, not the day, in chips was violent to the upside — SOXX +17.5%, AVGO +25.0% (+5.5% today), AMD +44.7% (+5.9%), MU +21.6%, TSM +14.8%, Taiwan's TAIEX +10.0% — and QQQ is +6.4% on the week. The AI complex is dispersing, not collapsing wholesale.

Defensive and health-care leadership is broad and accelerating rather than panicked: XLV +10.7% on the month (z=2.50, RS +13.8%), LLY +22.4%, XLP +8.2% (z=2.04), MCD z=3.04, HD z=2.51, COST +14.6%, UPS +16.4%. Money is rotating, not leaving.

Consumer cost relief is real: RBOB gasoline -19.7% on the month (z=-1.83) and the 30-year mortgage down 29bp to 7.11 with acceleration z=-2.36, even as crude holds — Brent 96.08, WTI 88.50 and both turning up.

bad.text: The dollar is maxed and it is the squeeze: DXY 103.25 at the 100th percentile (+3.6% in three months), EURUSD 1.1055 at the 0th, USDCHF at the 100th, AUDUSD -0.8% to 0.6787 (z=-1.09), EM currency basket CEW -0.6% and rolling over. Dollar composite -44.

Brazil is a genuine accident: USDBRL +1.5% to 5.6656, +12.7% on the month at z=3.62 with acceleration z=2.81 — the most extreme pair of readings on the board. EWZ -25.9% in a month (z=-3.37), Bovespa -17.2%, Argentina -18.1% and at the 0th percentile.

Crypto broke a round number: BTC 69,152 (-3.1%, -15.2% on the month), ETH through 2,000 to 1,955 (-19.1%), SOL -22.6%, IBIT -4.5%, MSTR -24.8%, COIN -28.1% and at the 0th percentile of its year. Real yields at 2.78 are the proximate cause.

The tail of credit keeps decompressing while the index tightens: CCC spreads +19bp today to 13.30, +77bp on the month, +445bp year-to-date, 95th percentile — a 1,000bp gap to the HY index. That split is a funding-cost problem working its way down the quality ladder.

Cyclical commodities flatly contradict the strong macro prints: copper -6.7% on the month and rolling over, COPX -3.3% today and -15.9% on the month, FCX -2.7%, XME -2.0%, REMX -4.2%, DBC at z=-1.75. Copper/gold is holding only because gold fell harder.

The rotation that was absorbing the AI unwind is now itself rolling: RSP/SPY -0.5% after stretching to z=3.10, IWM/SPY -1.3%, Russell 2000 -1.7%, and the month's winners hit hardest — JETS -3.8%, XRT -1.8%, ITB -1.8%, XHB -1.7%.

trades.name: LatAm dispersion: Mexico over Brazil
trades.line: Long EWW / short EWZ: Mexico compounds, Brazil is breaking
trades.expr: Equal dollar long EWW versus short EWZ. For a more convex version, buy 3-month USDBRL calls struck ~10% out of the money and fund partially by selling USDMXN calls.
trades.thesis: The dollar move is not hitting EM uniformly — it is hitting the weakest fiscal and carry stories. Brazil's currency and equity market are in a disorderly unwind; Mexico's are at the top of their range with a stable peso. The dispersion inside one region is cleaner and better funded than any outright EM directional bet.
trades.trigger: USDBRL +1.5% today to 5.6656, +12.7% on the month at z=3.62 with acceleration z=2.81; EWZ -25.9% on the month at z=-3.37 and Bovespa -17.2%. Against that, EWW +6.0% on the month, Mexico IPC at the 98th percentile, USDMXN -0.1% today.
trades.stop: USDBRL back below 5.35 (reversing the entire month's blowout), or the pair down 7%, or EWZ outperforming EWW for five consecutive sessions.
trades.target: EWW outperforms EWZ by 12%; USDBRL toward 6.00.

trades.name: Crypto equity proxies
trades.line: Short MSTR+COIN: bitcoin lost 70k, the proxies lag worse
trades.expr: Equal-weight short MSTR and COIN, or buy 2-month put spreads on each. Keep notional modest — both are 4-6% daily movers.
trades.thesis: Bitcoin has broken 70,000 with real yields at 2.78 and 24% above their 200-day. The equity proxies carry leverage and fee-income beta to the spot move, and historically decay faster than the coin on the way down. COIN at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range and MSTR 14% below its 200-day say the de-rating is already underway, not priced.
trades.trigger: BTC -3.1% to 69,152 and -15.2% on the month; ETH through 2,000 to 1,955 (-19.1%); SOL -22.6%; IBIT -4.5%; MSTR -6.5% on the day and -24.8% on the month; COIN -4.1% and -28.1% on the month.
trades.stop: Bitcoin reclaims 75,000, or the combined short loses 12%.
trades.target: 20% on the combined short, consistent with BTC toward 60,000.

trades.name: Low vol over high beta
trades.line: Long SPLV / short SPHB: beta loses as breadth rolls over
trades.expr: Dollar-neutral long SPLV versus short SPHB. Can be run alongside, not instead of, index exposure — it is the cheapest way to de-beta without selling the book.
trades.thesis: The index level is flattering a tape where leadership has narrowed into defensives. With funding costs rising and the small-cap/equal-weight rotation now failing, the factor that gets paid is low volatility and cash-flow stability, not operating leverage.
trades.trigger: SPHB/SPLV -15.5% on the month at z=-2.43 with acceleration z=-1.84; SPLV +7.1% on the month at z=1.92 and turning up; MTUM -11.4% at z=-2.13; RSP/SPY -0.5% after stretching to z=3.10 and IWM/SPY -1.3%; XLP z=2.04 and USMV at the 97th percentile.
trades.stop: SPHB/SPLV closes back above its 200-day (currently 6.6% above spot), or the pair loses 5%.

trades.name: Short the long end
trades.line: Short TLT: 30y at 5.35, real yield 2.78, core CPI turning up
trades.expr: Short TLT outright, or buy 3-month TLT 77 puts. Equivalent in futures: short ultra bond.
trades.thesis: The bond market is repricing a Fed that is done cutting and may have to go the other way, with inflation still grinding higher. Breakevens rose alongside yields, so this is a term-premium and policy repricing, not a growth bid for duration. MOVE at 98 and up 42% in three months means the volatility seller is not there to cap it.
trades.trigger: DGS30 +9bp to 5.35 and DGS2 +17bp to 4.73; the 3-month bill at 4.30 against 3.88 effective funds; DFII10 +12bp to 2.78 and 24.2% above its 200-day; 5-year breakevens +6bp to 2.31; TLT -1.5% on the day and -2.7% on the week with trend down.
trades.stop: TLT above 83 (roughly 10-year back below 4.75) — a 4% loss on the short.

trades.name: Energy equities over the index
trades.line: Long XLE vs SPY: energy bid on soft crude, Brent holds 96
trades.expr: Long XLE versus short SPY, equal dollars. Tilt the long toward integrateds (XOM, CVX) over refining exposure given gasoline's collapse.
trades.thesis: Energy equities rose on a day the index fell and on a month when crude fell 7-9%. That divergence — equities refusing to follow the commodity down — usually resolves with the commodity, not the equity. With Brent and WTI both turning up from 96.08 and 88.50 and the sector's three-month relative strength at +8.6% and rising, this is the only commodity-linked group with an up trend.
trades.trigger: XLE +1.5% and XOP +1.6% with SPX -0.4%; XOM +1.8%, CVX +1.4%; XLE 9.5% above its 200-day at the 79th percentile; Brent +0.3% today and turning up despite -9.4% on the month.
trades.stop: Brent below 88, or the pair down 6%.

trades.name: Semis dispersion snapback
trades.line: Long NVDA / short AMD: widest dispersion on the board
trades.expr: Equal dollar long NVDA versus short AMD. Smaller size than the other pairs — this fights an active momentum trend in AMD.
trades.thesis: Two stocks in the same supply chain, pricing opposite futures. NVDA sits at the 1.9th percentile of its 52-week range and 18.5% below its 200-day after a 27% monthly drawdown; AMD is 39.4% above its 200-day and +173% year-to-date. Nothing fundamental separated them by that much in four weeks. The spread, not the sector, is the trade.
trades.trigger: NVDA -4.3% to 166.19 (-8.5% on the week) while AMD +5.9% to 585.30 and +44.7% on the week; NVDA relative strength -25.3% on the month versus AMD -0.7%; SMH -1.0% and SOXX flat on the day, so this is idiosyncratic dispersion, not sector direction.
trades.stop: NVDA below 150, or the pair loses 10%.

trades.name: India over broad EM
trades.line: Long INDA / short EEM: India z=2.9 as EM funding tightens
trades.expr: Long INDA versus short EEM, equal dollars. Accept the ~20% India weight inside EEM — the residual short is Korea, Taiwan, China and Brazil, which is precisely the exposure to shed.
trades.thesis: A tightening dollar is a stock-pickers' sorting machine in EM. India has a strengthening currency, no dollar funding stress and an accelerating domestic tape; the rest of the EM index is Taiwan/Korea semiconductor beta rolling over, China at multi-year lows and Brazil in a currency crisis.
trades.trigger: Sensex +12.1% on the month at z=2.89 with acceleration z=2.59; INDA +9.1% at z=2.04 with relative strength +12.1% and turning up; USDINR -1.1% on the month and rolling over. Against that EEM -7.0% at z=-1.50, EEM/SPY -4.4%, KOSPI -12.0%, EWT -14.3%, KWEB -7.3%, EWZ -25.9%.
trades.stop: USDINR above 96, or the pair loses 5%.
